title: L2 grit unboxed: A meta-analytic journey into L2 grit and its correlates
matches.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>As an emerging field of study within second language acquisition (SLA), the notion of grit has gained immediate relevance as it is considered to play a key role in language achievement. Although recent years have witnessed increasing attention to second language (L2) grit due to its merits in foreign/second language learning processes, a comprehensive meta-analysis synthesizing the results of all available studies on the relationship between L2 grit and its frequently associated variables is currently lacking. Therefore, the current meta-analytic study scrutinized the total mean correlation between L2 grit and six main correlates examined in the research domain: foreign language enjoyment, L2 motivation, foreign language anxiety (FLA), ideal L2 self, growth mindset, and teacher support. A total of k = 34 effect sizes were analyzed with an overall sample size of N = 13,068 in random-effects models with correlation coefficients. The findings indicated that L2 motivation is the strongest correlate of L2 grit (r = .58), indicating a large effect size. The other five variables were moderately correlated with L2 grit, with FLA (r = −.47) being the strongest correlate and growth mindset (r = .33) being the weakest correlate. Implications of these findings and directions for future research are discussed.</jats:p>
